summary:
Voyage is an interactive 3D picture book designed for children aged 11–14, with the goal of making complex space exploration concepts easier, more engaging, and exciting to learn.

The platform features interactive 3D models of human-made hardware left on the Moon, Mars, and throughout outer space. Rather than simply displaying these objects, Voyage encourages users to explore their components and discover the science and engineering behind them.

To make learning rewarding, we implemented a progressive notes system. Information is introduced gradually, with more advanced notes unlocking as users progress through the picture book. This helps reduce the learning curve while creating a sense of accomplishment.

To capture children's attention, we also developed a Voyager Driving Simulator, allowing users to playfully navigate around the iconic spacecraft. It transforms an unconventional childhood fantasy into an opportunity to introduce real space exploration.

We built Voyage using React, React Three Fiber, Three.js, HTML, and vanilla CSS. AI tools assisted development, research, and audio generation, while Git supported version control and collaboration.

Our approach prioritizes feasibility, scalability, and educational impact. Ultimately, Voyage has two goals: to capture children's attention and to arouse their curiosity. We hope that a child who arrives wanting to drive a spacecraft leaves wanting to understand how it works.

details:
Its an interactive 3d picture book designed for children aged 11-14 years. To put simply, we wanted to help people, especially children, learn about complex topics in easier ways. We wanted their first experience with space to be exciting and more than anything: intriguing. It essentially uses 3d models of the hardware that has been left on the moon, mars and outer space.

But it doesn't just show the models. It gamifies the experience. How you ask? By using a simple notes feature. But it doesn't just dump information. We used an unlocking system where more complex notes unlock as you progress through the picture book, which we hope will create a sense of accomplishment and soften the learning curve.

The project has but two goals: to arouse their curiosity. But, first we needed to capture their attention. How could we achieve both?

Among many ways, we chose the approach of a Voyager Driving Simulator. Did your 10 year old self ever wish drive around Voyager 1 like a car game. This obviously raises a lot of questions. Voyager 1 isn't even abandoned. In fact, on November 18 it is reaching a grand milestone and people are preparing for it even, or at least I would hope so.

Its simply to fulfill the wish of driving around a spacecraft like a car. That is in fact all. And that is how we wish to actually hook the children.

We used r3f, three.js and react for the website design. Not to mention, vanilla css and html.

AI was used to aid the development process:
Claude was used for code completion and design.

ChatGPT was used for research.

Speechma and native web browser voice models were used for audio generation.

For coding, we used Visual Studio Code. And to store backups and boost team efficiency, we used Git.

How is our project creative? I don't know. We would like for you to be the judge of that.

We considered several factor including project feasibility, scaling and impact. Based upon them, we decided to go after this generic project.
